title: Austin's Pedestrian Safety & Social Funds
summary:
*   **Pedestrian Safety Funding Boost:** Council approved an allocation of quarter-cent transportation funds, including significant investments in pedestrian safety around areas like Lanier High School, though discussions highlighted ongoing concerns about equitable distribution of funds across all districts.
*   **Health & Human Services Budget Prioritized:** A policy goal was established to increase the Health and Human Services budget, aiming to address systemic inequalities and support vulnerable populations, despite some council members expressing reservations about setting budget directives outside the annual budget process.
*   **Downtown Public Restrooms Initiative:** The city manager was directed to investigate and propose solutions for public toilets in the downtown area, a move supported by community members citing public health, dignity, and environmental benefits.
*   **Water Resource Planning Contract Postponed:** A $1 million contract for integrated water resource planning was delayed to allow for a comprehensive review by an ad-hoc council group, ensuring alignment with long-term sustainability goals and consideration of innovative strategies.
*   **African-American Advisory Commission Changes:** Adjustments were made to the structure and membership of the African-American Resource Advisory Commission to enhance its effectiveness in addressing persistent disparities and quality of life issues within the community.

agenda_items.description: Approve the waiver or reimbursement of certain fees and requirements under City Code Chapter 14-8, and authorize payment of certain costs for the City cosponsored 2016 Martin Luther King Jr. parade which was held Monday, January 18, 2016.

Approve an ordinance waiving or reimbursing certain fees for the Chinese New Year Celebration sponsored by the Chinese Society of Austin which is to be held on Saturday, February 6, 2016 at the Asian American Resource Center.

Authorize reimbursement of certain costs under City Code Chapter 14-8 for the March for Gun-Free Campuses sponsored by Gun-Free UT which was held on Friday, January 8, 2016 beginning at the JW Marriott on East 2nd St. and ending at the Texas State Capitol building.

Approve an ordinance waiving development fees for the construction of accessible ramps for existing single-family and duplex residential dwelling units built by qualifying non-profit entities for income-eligible individuals.
Approve an ordinance amending City Code Chapter 2-1 relating to the African-American Resource Advisory Commission.
Approve an ordinance amending City Code Chapter 2-1 related to the Downtown Commission.
Approve a resolution directing the City Manager to partner with the Local Economies Council in hosting the annual Local Business Conference.

Item Referred from Health & Human Services Committee  Posting Language: Approve a resolution directing the City Manager to explore options and locations for the provision of safe, durable, 24-hour free public toilets.  BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AUSTIN: That the City Manager is directed to convene relevant Downtown stakeholders including the Austin Resource Center for the Homeless and Front Steps, Caritas, the Salvation Army, the American Association of Retired Persons, the Downtown Austin Alliance, the Waller Creek Conservancy, the downtown cluster of congregations Ã‚Â£uid social service providers, and other providers offering resources to the homeless, as well as relevant City departments, including the Development Services Department, Austin Water Utility, Health and Human Services Department, Austin Police Department, and Austin Resource Recovery to make recommendations about options, locations, and funding for the provision of safe, durable, 24-hour free public toilets.  BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED:  That the City Manager is directed to compile information on publicly accessible toilets located on City property in the Downtown area and report how the City might be able to make them available to the public 24 hours per day.  That the City Manager is directed to work with stakeholders to map the locations of all publicly accessible 24-hour toilets located on City property in the Downtown area.  That the City Manager shall report back to the Health and Human Services Committee at its March meeting with recommendations for moving forward with a pilot project for Downtown public toilets.
Approve a resolution initiating amendments to City Code Chapter 25-10 (Sign Regulations) relating to digital signage.   Council approved this item with significant amendments.

Conduct a public hearing and consider an ordinance amending City Code Title 25 relating to neighborhood plan contact team regulations.  Council conducted a public hearing and approved an ordinance on all three readings (Ordinance No 20160128-084) with direction to bring the proposed by-laws back to Council for further debate and input.  *Related to CIUR 1656
